items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to receive the claimed refund
items.quote: überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for payment: 'bis zum 27.11.2026'. No period to count, no deemed-delivery rule applies since no payment is actually owed by law here; the date is simply as stated in the letter.

warnings: This letter shows strong hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: an unsolicited, unusually generous 'refund' (612,00 €) is dangled, but you are asked to pay a smaller 'processing fee' (49,90 €) up front before the refund is released - a classic 419/advance-fee fraud pattern, not how real German energy refunds work.

The sender claims to be a German consumer body ('Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie') but its postal address and phone number are in Nicosia, Cyprus, which does not match a genuine German consumer-protection authority.

The payee IBAN (CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600) is a Cypriot account; a legitimate German energy-cost refund would not require payment to a foreign account before paying out, and the IBAN being technically well-formed says nothing about who actually controls it.
The letter uses pressure tactics ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig.') to rush payment within about a week - a common scam technique.
No real company, contract, meter, or supplier details tie this 'refund' to any actual energy account of the recipient; do not transfer any money and do not click any links or reply with bank details.

Recommendation: do not pay the requested fee; verify independently (e.g. via Verbraucherzentrale NRW or your actual energy supplier) before taking any action, and consider reporting this letter as a scam.
